text: Lois Lowry's The Giver was challenged in Palm Springs, where a library clerk and principal objected to it as inappropriate for a fourth-grade reading class and requested its removal from district elementary school libraries and classrooms. The school board upheld the assistant superintendent’s decision to remove it from those libraries and move it to middle school and high school libraries. In 1996 it was challenged at Glacier Gateway Elementary School in Columbia Falls over questionable values and concerns that it would desensitize students to murder, suicide and infanticide, and it was retained. In Elk Grove, an objector requested the removal of The Giver and other materials assigned to a seventh-grade class, alleging that they contained “negative situations” conflicting with “personal moral convictions” and claiming that they aimed to “brainwash” students.
meta_description: The Giver by Lois Lowry: challenged in Palm Springs, Columbia Falls (1996) and Elk Grove; moved to higher-grade libraries in one case, retained in another.
changes: Author-led opening; the Palm Springs case split into objection and board decision; dated 1996 case kept.
